_comment: Which of the six Form I babs a p~q vowel code names, and its display name. p is the past vowel, q the present vowel, read off Wiktionary's ar-verb template (I/a~u etc).
_form_keys: Wiktionary spells the two quadriliteral forms lowercase; patterns.json keys them uppercase. Only the forms that differ need an entry.
_hollow: A أجوف root is found under its past (غيب under غَابَ), and its weak letter rules out one present vowel: the present's middle vowel is that letter come back, يَقُولُ from و and يَبِيعُ from ي (Treasures pp.180-190). Weak letter -> the present vowel it never takes.
_hollow_alif: A hollow past whose present takes a fatha (خَافَ يَخَافُ, هَابَ يَهَابُ) is سَمِعَ: the alif hides a kasra, خَوِفَ يَخْوَفُ, as Lane itself writes. Read as fathas it would be a~a, a bab hollow verbs never take.
_sources: Where a verb's bab can come from. Every source in this order is tried and every one that answers is shown, so a reader sees both books when both name one.
